argument_summary: No new evidence is added. On the admissible record alone, the strongest supportable defense is narrower than clean certification: the release is operationally supportable on aggregate readiness because it clears launch readiness by 2.2 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance supports launch decisions that document limitations and monitor residual risk across deployment. The main dispute is not whether the system is broadly launch-ready, but whether the named disability accommodations gap requires pre-launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance before certification is treated as fully compliant. Because the record shows a 1.2 point miss, names the segment in two accommodation commitments, and leaves legal review open, the better reading is caveated compliance rather than a broader noncompliance finding that forces escalation beyond the existing packet.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the semester-services launch path, but business cost is not offered as a policy override. At most, the product note that the affected segment is 5% of projected first-month traffic supports a risk-weighted view that the issue is limited in immediate operational scope while governance closure proceeds.
claims_about_policy: The admissible evidence does not show that general model-card or AI-risk-management guidance overrides the release policy. The narrower policy claim is that those sources support certification with documented limitations and monitoring when the policy predicates are otherwise satisfied or are being handled through the required governance path. The current record supports aggregate readiness and residual-risk monitoring, but it leaves unresolved whether the named-use-case limitation has been disclosed or formally accepted. That unresolved point justifies a caveat; it does not require treating the entire certification basis as unsupported.
concessions: The disability accommodations intake segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points.
That segment is named in two university accommodation commitments, which weighs toward materiality under the stated policy and policy text.
The legal review on disclosure remains open.
There is no admissible evidence of completed disclosure or approved pre-launch risk acceptance in the present record.
The 5% projected traffic note does not by itself resolve materiality.
